title: Quasi-isomorphisms between colimits of resolving towers survive the functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with cochain, homotopy and derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in an ambient universe. Assume sequential colimits exist in both categories and preserve short exact sequences of diagrams in $\mathcal B$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and preserve sequential colimits. Let $\mathcal P$ contain $0$, be closed under finite direct sums, and cover every object of $\mathcal A$ by an epimorphism from an object of $\mathcal P$. Suppose $F(C)$ is acyclic for every bounded above acyclic complex $C$ with terms in $\mathcal P$. Define $\overline{\mathcal P}$ as the class of objects isomorphic to objects of $\mathcal P$. For each $n\ge1$, let $E_n,G_n$ be bounded above complexes with terms in $\overline{\mathcal P}$ and transitions $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and $v_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$. Suppose compatible cocones $e_n:E_n\to X$ and $g_n:G_n\to Y$ exhibit $X,Y$ as their respective termwise sequential colimits. Assume $H^j(E_n)=H^j(G_n)=0$ for $j>n$, and $H^j(e_n),H^j(g_n)$ are isomorphisms for $j\le n$. Then for every quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:X\to Y$, the chain map $F(\alpha):F(X)\to F(Y)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The morphism $\alpha$ is arbitrary; it need not be induced by a map of the two towers.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, first-paragraph cone argument and the claim beginning “Suppose that”, through the final cohomology-colimit calculation. Includes transfer of the acyclicity assumption to the isomorphism closure.

proof.text: The class $\overline{\mathcal P}$ contains zero, is closed under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and still covers every object by an epimorphism. For an acyclic bounded above $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complex $C$, choose degreewise isomorphisms $a^r:P^r\simeq C^r$ with $P^r\in\mathcal P$, choosing $P^r=0$ above a bound. Give $P$ differential $(a^{r+1})^{-1}d_C^ra^r$. These differentials square to zero and $a:P\simeq C$ is a complex isomorphism. Functoriality of cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $P$ acyclic. The hypothesis makes $F(P)$ acyclic, and the complex isomorphism $F(a)$ makes $F(C)$ acyclic. For closure under sums, if $M\simeq P$ and $N\simeq Q$, the biproduct of these isomorphisms identifies $M\oplus N$ with $P\oplus Q\in\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, first paragraph and proof of the claim, ending with the cohomology-colimit calculation.

proof.text: Let $s:C\to D$ be any quasi-isomorphism between bounded above $\overline{\mathcal P}$-complexes. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], its cone is acyclic. The cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives terms $D^r\oplus C^{r+1}$, so this cone is bounded above and has terms in $\overline{\mathcal P}$. Step 1 makes $F(C(s))$ acyclic. An additive functor preserves the finite biproduct with its inclusions and projections; under $F(D^r\oplus C^{r+1})\simeq F(D^r)\oplus F(C^{r+1})$, the differential matrix becomes $\begin{pmatrix}F(d_D)&F(s)\\0&-F(d_C)\end{pmatrix}$. Hence $F(C(s))\simeq C(F(s))$, and a second application of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] shows that $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, first paragraph and proof of the claim, ending with the cohomology-colimit calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-stage-roof-comparison] to $\overline{\mathcal P}$ and $F$. Step 1 verifies the zero, isomorphism, finite-biproduct and epimorphic-cover assumptions; Step 2 verifies preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between bounded above complexes in this class. All the tower, augmentation, vanishing and cohomology-isomorphism assumptions are precisely the hypotheses of the present item. For the given arbitrary quasi-isomorphism $\alpha$, obtain isomorphisms $\theta_n^i:H^i(F(E_n))\simeq H^i(F(G_n))$ with $\theta_{n+1}^iH^i(F(u_n))=H^i(F(v_n))\theta_n^i$ and $H^i(F(g_n))\theta_n^i=H^i(F(\alpha))H^i(F(e_n))$. This invocation does not require a morphism of towers inducing $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, first paragraph and proof of the claim, ending with the cohomology-colimit calculation.

proof.text: The cocones $F(e_n)$ and $F(g_n)$ are termwise sequential colimits because $F$ preserves such colimits. They are also colimits of complexes: the universal degreewise maps commute with differentials since they do so after precomposition with every cocone leg, which jointly determine maps by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Apply [src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits] in $\mathcal B$, with index category the small ordered set of positive integers and cochain shape $\mathbf Z$. Its existence and exactness hypotheses are exactly the assumed sequential-colimit hypotheses in $\mathcal B$. Thus $H^i(F(X))$ and $H^i(F(Y))$, with legs $H^i(F(e_n))$ and $H^i(F(g_n))$, are colimits of the two cohomology diagrams for every $i$. No exactness of sequential colimits in $\mathcal A$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0794, proposition-left-derived-exists, first paragraph and proof of the claim, ending with the cohomology-colimit calculation.

proof.text: Fix $i$. The compatible inverses of the isomorphisms in Step 3 satisfy $H^i(F(u_n))(\theta_n^i)^{-1}=(\theta_{n+1}^i)^{-1}H^i(F(v_n))$. By the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and Step 4, the compatible legs $H^i(F(e_n))(\theta_n^i)^{-1}$ define $\beta_i:H^i(F(Y))\to H^i(F(X))$. Step 3's augmentation identity implies $\beta_iH^i(F(\alpha))H^i(F(e_n))=H^i(F(e_n))$ and $H^i(F(\alpha))\beta_iH^i(F(g_n))=H^i(F(g_n))$. Colimit uniqueness gives $\beta_iH^i(F(\alpha))=1$ and $H^i(F(\alpha))\beta_i=1$. Therefore every $H^i(F(\alpha))$ is invertible, which is the definition of a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The item states the Claim at 9383-9394, plus the first-paragraph cone argument, and asks for exact colimits only in B. Its statement is unchanged from the live base, and there is no repair note, so the re-split rule does not apply. There are no new nodes. Step 1 (elementary): conjugating the differentials moves the acyclicity hypothesis to the isomorphism closure P-bar, and P-bar keeps zero, biproducts and the epimorphic cover. Step 2: lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic in both directions, with the cone formula C(f)^r=L^r+K^{r+1} from def-weil-abstract-derived-category; an additive F gives F(C(s)) iso to C(F(s)), so F preserves quasi-isomorphisms between bounded-above P-bar complexes. Step 3: every hypothesis of lem-trf-bounded-stage-roof-comparison checked (P-bar iso-closed, quasi-isomorphism preservation from step 2, towers, augmentations, the j>n and j<=n conditions, alpha arbitrary). Its output, theta_n with both identities, is exactly what the step uses. That node assumes no colimits, so it is strictly smaller than the item, and its proof_deps do not lead back to the item (no cycle). Step 4: the termwise colimit cocone is a colimit of complexes by uniqueness from the colimit definition, and src-weil-homology-preserves-exact-colimits applies with I = positive integers and shape Z in B; 'preserves short exact sequences' equals 'exact' because colim is already right exact. Step 5: checked the cocone condition for the legs H(Fe_n)theta_n^-1, both inverse identities after composing with the legs, and colimit uniqueness, so every H^i(F alpha) is invertible. proof_deps equal the union of the uses. A DAG search for 0794, resolving towers and the citers found no duplicate. Accepted the two generic tool_uses (cone-acyclic, homology-preserves-exact-colimits). No SGA source. Small cases: F=0, F=id with alpha=id, P={0}, a single-degree complex, and tensoring with Z/2 on free abelian groups. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem resolution_colimit_quasiIso {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ B] [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesColimitsOfShape ℕ F] (P : A → Prop) (hzero : P (0 : A)) (hsum : ∀ (M N : A), P M → P N → P (M ⊞ N)) (hcover : ∀ M : A, ∃ (N : A) (p : N ⟶ M), P N ∧ Epi p) (hF : ∀ K : CochainComplex A ℤ, (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (K.X j)) → (∀ j : ℤ, P (K.X j)) → K.Acyclic → ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K).Acyclic) (E G : ℕ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) (hEbound : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero ((E.obj k).X j)) (hGbound : ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero ((G.obj k).X j)) (hEterms : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), ∃ M : A, P M ∧ Nonempty (M ≅ (E.obj k).X j)) (hGterms : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), ∃ M : A, P M ∧ Nonempty (M ≅ (G.obj k).X j)) (X Y : CochainComplex A ℤ) (e : E ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj X) (g : G ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj Y) (hecolim : ∀ j : ℤ, IsColimit ((HomologicalComplex.eval A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) j).mapCocone (Cocone.mk X e))) (hgcolim : ∀ j : ℤ, IsColimit ((HomologicalComplex.eval A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) j).mapCocone (Cocone.mk Y g))) (hEvanish : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), (k : ℤ) + 1 < j → IsZero ((E.obj k).homology j)) (hGvanish : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), (k : ℤ) + 1 < j → IsZero ((G.obj k).homology j)) (heiso : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), j ≤ (k : ℤ) + 1 → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (e.app k) j)) (hgiso : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : ℤ), j ≤ (k : ℤ) + 1 → IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (g.app k) j)) (α : X ⟶ Y) (hα : QuasiIso α) : QuasiIso ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map α)
